sources.title: From Crisis to Recovery: Local Authorities Confronting Post-War Realities in Lebanon: Rapid Impact Assessment
geographic_coverage: 135 surveyed affected areas in 19 districts and eight governorates
sources.temporal_coverage: Hostilities October 2023–November 2024; municipality survey 5–15 December 2024; publication January 2025.
sources.methodology: Municipal self-survey of 135 affected areas, coordinated with governorate disaster-risk units, plus four local deep dives, displacement records and a November 2024 perceptions survey.
sources.limitations: About 34% of affected areas responded; 62 mostly southern-border areas were hard to reach. Estimates are preliminary and unvalidated; some damage may predate September 2024.

sources.title: The Socioeconomic Impacts of the 2024 War on Lebanon
sources.organization: United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA), UNDP, UNICEF, ILO and UN-Habitat
sources.temporal_coverage: 2024 war impacts; field data collected December 2024–February 2025; publication July 2025.
sources.methodology: Joint UN analysis of field surveys, satellite damage data and sector studies.
sources.limitations: Desk review supplements primary data; projection scenario is unspecified.

sources.title: FAO and Ministry of Agriculture Launch the Lebanon Agricultural Damage and Loss Assessment Report
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), Ministry of Agriculture and National Council for Scientific Research-Lebanon
sources.temporal_coverage: Conflict assessment period October 2023–November 2024; recovery priorities include 2025/26.
sources.methodology: Official FAO launch summary of a DIEM-Impact agricultural damage-and-loss assessment conducted with the Ministry of Agriculture and CNRS-L.
sources.limitations: Only the official launch summary was inspected; the linked full report was inaccessible, so no unreported tables or localities are asserted.

claims.paraphrase: At the report date, UNDP described post-war recovery as constrained by institutional capacity weakened by prolonged fiscal and economic shocks, a political vacuum, and conditions restricting external aid.
claims.limitations: Post-ceasefire assessment of conditions in 2024–January 2025, not a current 2026 measure or causal evaluation.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report says political vacuum and instability conditions hampered response and constrained aid access.

claims.locator: PDF pp.7–8/16, agricultural assets and municipal facilities
claims.paraphrase: Across surveyed areas, 14,762 agricultural assets were reported damaged; Baalbek and Bint Jbeil had the highest counts, while Nabatieh and Sour had high complete-damage shares. Consultations also raised water contamination, ecosystem, debris and soil-restoration concerns.
claims.limitations: Municipality-reported sample findings; consultations did not geographically allocate each environmental concern.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report attributes these damage and recovery concerns to the war.

claims.locator: Printed p.45, regional labour-market disparities and climate challenges
claims.paraphrase: Conflict-affected Bekaa and southern Lebanon are projected to face end-century wet-bulb globe temperature increases of 2–3.5°C; without adaptation, heat would reduce labour capacity, especially for outdoor manual workers.
claims.scenario: Source-unspecified; the report gives an end-of-century projection but no emissions pathway.
claims.limitations: Regional projection, not district-specific; adaptation response is not evaluated.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report says climate challenges compound labour-market disparities in conflict-affected areas.

claims.locator: Printed pp.49–50, disruption in access to utilities
claims.paraphrase: Attacks damaged at least 34 water facilities, affecting over 400,000 people; climate-related pressures already strained supply. In Rmeich, disrupted access affected about 1,325 households, including 175 displaced families.
claims.limitations: Occupation restricted full inspection; the report does not disaggregate climate-driven losses for each locality.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The report explicitly says attacks exacerbated water pressures it attributes to climate change.

claims.paraphrase: The report says military operations damaged natural habitats and coastal ecosystems, increasing Lebanon's vulnerability to climate change and biodiversity loss.
claims.limitations: National-level synthesis; this passage does not locate specific damaged ecosystems.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: War-caused ecosystem damage is explicitly linked to greater climate vulnerability.

claims.locator: Official FAO launch page, assessment findings and recovery priorities
claims.paraphrase: The FAO–Ministry–CNRS-L assessment attributes 2023–2024 agricultural impacts to conflict and estimates US$118 million in damage and US$586 million in losses, with Southern Lebanon and Bekaa most affected.
claims.limitations: Figures and geographic detail are from the official launch summary, not the inaccessible full report.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: The launch page identifies conflict as the cause of the assessed sector impacts.

claims.locator: Official FAO launch page, recovery needs and medium-term priorities
claims.paraphrase: The release estimates US$263 million in agricultural recovery needs, with US$95 million prioritized for 2025/26; proposed actions include restoring farms, irrigation systems, greenhouses, machinery and natural-resource management.
claims.limitations: Needs and actions are recommendations, not evidence that recovery capacity or outcomes were delivered.

search_audit.query: Lebanon subnational climate risks in conflict-affected Bekaa and southern Lebanon, local water and agricultural vulnerability, primary UN reports
search_audit.outcome: Found full joint ESCWA–UNDP analysis with named regional heat and water interactions, local Rmeich impact, and UNDP municipal assessment; local climate projections remain regional rather than district-specific.

search_audit.query: Lebanon primary evidence climate change, conflict, water scarcity, labour and local social vulnerability mediators
search_audit.outcome: Full joint report explicitly links climate challenges to labour-market vulnerability in conflict-affected areas and says attacks worsened climate-related water pressures; existing baseline also covers perceived tensions and one local water-dialogue case.

search_audit.query: Lebanon conflict damage to climate resilience, water systems, ecosystems and agricultural livelihoods primary reports
search_audit.outcome: Joint UN report documents conflict-related water and ecosystem damage, inability to operate or repair some facilities, and explicit worsening of climate-related water stress; it does not evaluate obstruction of climate-adaptation projects.

search_audit.query: Lebanon local recovery capacity municipal services agriculture irrigation climate-smart restoration 2024-2026 official assessments
search_audit.outcome: UNDP municipal report records weakened capacity, political and aid constraints, and local service recovery needs; FAO summary gives agricultural recovery priorities, which remain plans rather than evaluated outcomes.

gaps: UNDP's municipal survey represents 135 of 392 affected areas; 62 hard-to-reach areas were mostly southern border villages, and reported damage was preliminary and unvalidated.
The full FAO agriculture assessment could not be accessed through its official report endpoint (403) or a government-hosted mirror (502); claims are limited to the FAO launch summary.

No reviewed source evaluates the effects of insecurity on delivery or effectiveness of climate-adaptation programs; conflict-to-climate interactions are documented for water and ecosystems, not as a causal climate-induced violence finding.
The joint UN report's heat projection is regional and its emissions scenario is unspecified; do not treat 2024–2025 findings or policy recommendations as current 2026 outcomes.
